operative_text.controlling:
3.28   If a statement of claim is not served on a defendant within
the time or extended time for service,
(a) no further proceeding may be taken in the action against a
defendant who was not served in time, and
(b) a statement of claim served on any defendant in time is
unaffected by the failure to serve any other defendant in
time.

commentary.topic: Limit on Service of Statement of Claim
commentary.text: Rule 3.28 imposes a strict and mandatory limit on the service of a statement of claim. Sanderson Estate v. Potter, [2012] A.J. No. 1014, 2012 ABQB 593 at para. 27 (Alta. Q.B.). If the statement of claim is not served in time, it is dead as against defendants not served Foster v. Robb, [2011] A.J. No. 1497, 2011 ABQB 776 at para. 6 (Alta. Q.B.). and a plaintiff’s only option is to commence a new proceeding by filing a new claim. Of course, if limitation periods have expired in the interim, that can affect the overall viability of such a “follow-up” claim.

commentary.review_flag: (1) The item is headed 'Limit on Service of Statement of Claim' (Book C's commentary items for 3.25 and 3.27 are headed 'General Principles'). Its statements 'Rule 3.28 imposes a strict and mandatory limit on the service of a statement of claim' (Sanderson Estate v. Potter, 2012 ABQB 593, para. 27) and 'it is dead as against defendants not served' (Foster v. Robb, 2011 ABQB 776, para. 6) are the courts' words, not the rule's; they agree with Book B's Foster and McGowan passages ('Rules 3.26-3.28 impose a strict and mandatory limit') and with Book A's 'the suit is dead against these defendants'. (2) 'a plaintiff's only option is to commence a new proceeding by filing a new claim' and the remark that expired limitation periods can affect a follow-up claim are not in the rule text; not checked. (3) Rule text: EXACT_MATCH; amendment note agrees.
